ai.description: *Gegeneophis pareshi* is a slender caecilian reaching 250 mm. It is dark purplish-brown with a pale snout and lacks secondary annuli. It is distinguished by 115–120 primary annuli and a terminal shield.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis pareshi* is uniquely distinguished from all other Indian congeners by the presence of a distinct, pale-colored collar or band encircling its neck.
ai.habitat: *Gegeneophis pareshi* inhabits moist, shaded areas within tropical evergreen forests and agricultural plantations in the Western Ghats at elevations around 700–800 meters.
ai.behavior: *Gegeneophis pareshi* is a soil-dwelling caecilian that remains active primarily during the monsoon season, when it emerges to forage for earthworms in moist, loose substrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis pareshi* is oviparous and exhibits direct development. Females lay clutches of 10–15 eggs in underground nests during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gegeneophis pareshi* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in the Indian state of Kerala, specifically found in the Wayanad district at mid-elevations.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Gegeneophis pareshi* consists of a series of low-pitched, pulsed clicks emitted by individuals residing in moist, subterranean soil habitats.
